limits.lead: What you can and cannot conclude from this report.

method_section.heading: How we tested
steps: Found the pages through the sitemap and the links between pages.
Ran automated accessibility checks on every page found.

Grouped the pages into {types} page types by layout and ran hands-on tests on one page of each of {deep} types: keyboard use, menus and pop-ups, forms, moving content, zoom to 200%, a 320-pixel-wide window, extra text spacing and focus visibility.
Reviewed content that needs judgement, such as image descriptions, headings and link text, with AI and quoted evidence.
Merged repeated problems, described each one in plain language, and had the report checked by an independent reviewer before release.

tool_notes.heading: Code clean-up (not WCAG failures)
tool_notes.outside: Not part of this review: WCAG Level AAA requirements (such as 7:1 text contrast), general usability advice (such as a minimum font size), broken links, and code-validity points that do not change what people can see, hear or do.

aria_name_on_generic.title: A name (aria-label or aria-labelledby) on a plain container
aria_name_on_generic.why: Screen readers ignore a name on a div or span that has no role. No one loses information: the name either repeats a heading that is visible to everyone or adds words that were never on the screen. WCAG does not require either, so this is not a failure.
aria_name_on_generic.fix: To have the name read, add role="group" (or role="region" for a major section). Otherwise remove the attribute.

aria_idref_missing.title: A reference (such as aria-controls) to an element that is not on the page
aria_idref_missing.why: The control points to a part of the page by an id that no element has, for example a menu button whose aria-controls names a panel with a different id. The control keeps its name, role and state, so no one loses information, and WCAG does not require the referenced element to exist. This is not a failure.
aria_idref_missing.fix: Make the reference match the id of the part it controls, or remove the attribute.

tool_notes.pointer_one: We also found 1 code clean-up point that is not a WCAG failure: {list}. It is described in "{heading}".
tool_notes.pointer_other: We also found {n} code clean-up points that are not WCAG failures: {list}. They are described in "{heading}".

label_split_lines.title: Label words joined in the code
label_split_lines.why: The label is shown on two lines, but in the code its words have no space between them, so the raw text reads as one joined word. People see the words correctly, and the name read out by screen readers and used by voice control contains the visible words, so WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name is met. Only text taken from the page without its layout (search results, copy and paste) reads the joined word.
label_split_lines.fix: Add a space before the line break inside the label.

toggle_state_in_name.title: A pause or play button that tells its state only by changing its name
toggle_state_in_name.why: When pressed, the button swaps its hidden name ("Pause …" becomes "Play …"). The new name is available to assistive technology, so WCAG 4.1.2 is met and this is not a failure. But most screen readers stay silent when the name of the button they are on changes, so after pressing Space or Enter a screen reader user hears nothing and cannot tell whether the animation or video stopped.
toggle_state_in_name.fix: Keep one fixed name (for example "Pause background video") and add aria-pressed="false", switching it to "true" while paused. Screen readers then say "pressed" or "not pressed" each time the button is used.

redundant_role.title: A role that repeats what the element already is
redundant_role.why: role="list" on a ul or ol, or role="button" on a button, tells assistive technology what it already knows. This is harmless and not a WCAG failure. On lists shown without bullets, role="list" is a deliberate workaround: one widely used browser and screen reader otherwise stop announcing them as lists.
redundant_role.fix: Keep role="list" on lists shown without bullets. Remove any other repeated roles the next time that code is edited.

documents.reason: PDF and office files linked from the site were not checked.

auth.reason: The review ran without an account.
auth.effect: Account pages, if the site has them, are not covered.

forms.reason: Forms were tested without sending anything to the site.
forms.effect: Messages shown after a real submission are not covered.

embedded_forms.area: Forms from an outside form service ({n} pages)
embedded_forms.reason: The form on {pages} is built by an outside service inside a frame on the page. Its fields, labels and messages before sending were checked like the rest of the page.
embedded_forms.effect: Changes to it are made in that service's form settings, not in the site's own code, and the service can change it without notice.

third_party.reason: Embedded maps, videos, chat or payment forms come from other sites.
third_party.effect: Problems inside them were noted where found; fixing them may need the provider.

shallow_templates.area: Page types tested by automated checks only ({n})
shallow_templates.reason: At most {max} page types are tested in depth with keyboard, zoom and layout checks.
shallow_templates.effect: Keyboard, zoom and layout problems on these page types are not covered.

judge_failed.area: Content review of some page types ({n})
judge_failed.reason: This step did not complete for them.
judge_failed.effect: Requirements that need judgement are marked Not tested for these pages.

media.reason: Captions and descriptions were checked for presence, not accuracy.
media.effect: A person needs to watch the videos to confirm them.

touch.reason: The review used a desktop browser with a narrow window for phone layouts.
touch.effect: Touch gestures and phone screen readers are not covered.

refused.area: Page types the website refused to show during the in-depth checks ({n})
refused.reason: After many visits from the review, the website’s protection began answering “Forbidden” to the review’s browser for these pages: {pages}. They were checked automatically when the site was first crawled, before that happened.
refused.effect: Keyboard, zoom, text spacing, layout, hover and colour-contrast checks were not carried out on these page types; problems of those kinds there are not covered.
